body.p: , after , , , , , , , . src/xslt_lower_number.c (rule view sxml_xslt_instruction_rules_number, one line in src/xslt_lower.c), tests/xslt_number_test.c; additive edits to src/format.c, src/function_library_format.c, src/function_library_xslt.c, src/xpath_lower.c and src/function_library_internal.h; no IR kind, no evaluator change, no public header.

item.p: xsl:number (12) is 12.3's formal definition as XPath texts with their inputs as variables ('s way): the selected node (XTTE0990, also for an absent focus, XTTE1000), the nodes count is tried on (the ancestors-or-self and their preceding siblings; for level="any" the preceding nodes and the ancestors-or-self), a FILTER of them by the count pattern's match expression (, inline, the item as fixed focus, an error is no match, 6.5; without count, a text for the selected node's kind and name), the same for from (on the ancestors-or-self, or the any-level candidates), then one text per level: matches-from's root case is (from | root($s))[last()], a counted node's preceding siblings are the counted candidates with its parent before it. value (12.2) is xs:integer(round(number(.))), exact for xs:decimal, XTDE0980; start-at (12.1) re-bases in a text (XTDE0030); XTSE0975 statically.

Formatting is one internal row, format-place-marker (src/xslt_number_internal.h, defined beside fn:format-integer), over 's engine: src/format.c splits the format into prefix, format tokens with their separators (". " before a number formatted by the first token) and suffix, and sxml_integer_formatting gained grouping-separator/grouping-size (a string every N digits of a decimal representation). An unparsable token is "1" (12.4). Ordinal: any value but "", no, 0, false. lang (xs:language or "") and letter-value (alphabetic, traditional) are checked (XTDE0030) and otherwise ignored: English only (). An empty place marker gives prefix and suffix (Saxon's behaviour; QT4 number-0806, -3205 expect it). Title-case words are "Twenty Two" here (Saxon's; number-0105, -2506), "Twenty-two" in fn:format-integer.

xsl:analyze-string (17.1) is fn:matching-segments (one regex engine, , ) of the select value coerced to xs:string?, the non-matching segments put between the matches by an XPath text (strings; matches stay fn:matching-segment-records), inside a TRY_CATCH mapping FORX0002/0001 to XTDE1140/1145; then a MAP over the segments whose body is a CONDITIONAL of the two children (select or sequence constructor) with the segment's string as context item in a slot of its own and the MAP's position and size. XTSE1130, XTSE1132, XTSE3185. compiled-regex is UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE.

Captured groups, a context variable (glossary): a new parameter default SXML_PARAMETER_DEFAULT_CONTEXT_VARIABLE makes the caller pass the variable Q{XSLT}N (N the parameter's name) lexically in scope, or () (captured from an inline function only when captured; a function item of the shorter arity captures it, so regex-group#1 keeps the groups, 17.2.2). xsl:matching-substring has Q{XSLT}regex-groups = the segment's groups map with entry 0 (value, position, nr 0) first; xsl:non-matching-substring has (). fn:regex-groups and fn:regex-group (rows of the xslt part) read it; regex-group(N) also finds a named group by its nr (analyze-string-406, as XSLT 3.0 had it). 4.9's context functions (current-group and the others, ) can use the same default instead of a second mechanism.

Measured with a scratch harness (lower, evaluate, serialize; XPath assertions through sxml xpath) over the in-scope cases (; the combinations_for_numbering ones are not): insn-number 152/161, insn-analyze-string 56/62, misc-regex 64/65, fn-format-number 67/70 (with 4.12's decimal formats); before the packet none of the instructions lowered. Of the rest: German words (6), Unicode digit sequences, the four dynamic-scope cases below, xsl:sort under xsl:number's callers, an attribute-set case.

Deviations: the captured groups are lexical, so a template called from xsl:matching-substring sees none (17.2 says they pass through apply-templates and call-template; QT4 analyze-string-078 to -081): an implicit tunnel parameter would carry them (src/xslt_lower_template.c). A start-at known statically is checked when evaluated (XTDE0030, not XTSE0020, number-0109). German and other languages, the Unicode numbering sequences (circled digits, number-0819..0821, out of scope by combinations_for_numbering otherwise) and traditional letter values fall back to the token "1" or English.
